items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I heard the trumpetist Ray Copeland and Jerome Richardson, the reed man, for the first time.

ctx.x: Of course I saw many of my musician friends and buddies because I went to Beefsteak Charlie's bar which was an old hangout for many of the gang that I knew before going to Europe. Some of the gang could be found in the Turf bar on Broadway and I went there a few times in the afternoon.

Oscar Pettiford opened a club on 3rd Avenue East side, called the Black Pearl and I was there on opening night with Lily of course. I heard the trumpetist Ray Copeland and Jerome Richardson, the reed man, for the first time. They were both fine musicians and Oscar found time now and then to knock out a few tunes on the bass. It was a very nice club but I heard that it did not stay open very long.

We left New York by train the 14th of March. George Duvivier drove us to the New York Central station in his Cadillac and we arrived in Cincinnati the next morning. The air conditioning system had been out of order and the heat was unbearable. We couldn't drink because the drinking water tank was empty and nobody came through selling drinks. We were more than happy to get out of that train.
